【DB_ID】 card_games
【Schema】
# Table: cards
[
(id:INTEGER, unique id number identifying the cards: -, Primary Key, Examples: [41138, 1349, 23810]),
(artist:TEXT, : The name of the artist that illustrated the card art.-, Examples: [Pete Venters, Volkan Baǵa, Justin Sweet]),
(asciiName:TEXT, ascii Name: The ASCII(opens new window) (Basic/128) code formatted card name with no special unicode characters.-, Examples: [El-Hajjaj, Junun Efreet, Dandan]),
(availability:TEXT, : A list of the card's available printing types.-"arena", "dreamcast", "mtgo", "paper", "shandalar", Examples: [mtgo,paper, paper, arena]),
(borderColor:TEXT, border Color: The color of the card border.-"black", "borderless", "gold", "silver", "white", Examples: [black, white, borderless]),
(cardKingdomFoilId:TEXT, card Kingdom Foil Id: card Kingdom Foil Id-cardKingdomFoilId, when paired with cardKingdomId that is not Null, is incredibly powerful., Examples: [123094, 123095, 123096]),
(cardKingdomId:TEXT, card Kingdom Id: card Kingdom Id-A list of all the colors in the color indicator, Examples: [122719, 122720, 122725]),
(colorIdentity:TEXT, color Identity: A list of all the colors found in manaCost, colorIndicator, and text-, Examples: [W, B, U]),
(colorIndicator:TEXT, color Indicator: A list of all the colors in the color indicator (The symbol prefixed to a card's types).-, Examples: [U, G, R]),
(colors:TEXT, : A list of all the colors in manaCost and colorIndicator.-Some cards may not have values, such as cards with "Devoid" in its text., Examples: [W, B, U]),
(convertedManaCost:REAL, converted Mana Cost: The converted mana cost of the card. Use the manaValue property.-if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana, Examples: [7.0, 5.0, 4.0]),
(duelDeck:TEXT, duel Deck: The indicator for which duel deck the card is in.-, Examples: [a, b]),
(edhrecRank:INTEGER, rec Rank in edh: The card rank on EDHRec-, Examples: [15650, 12702, 11081]),
(faceConvertedManaCost:REAL, face Converted Mana Cost: The converted mana cost or mana value for the face for either half or part of the card.-if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana for the face, Examples: [4.0, 5.0, 6.0]),
(faceName:TEXT, face Name: The name on the face of the card.-, Examples: [Dusk, Dawn, Commit]),
(flavorName:TEXT, flavor Name: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function.-The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function., Examples: [Godzilla, King of the Monsters]),
(flavorText:TEXT, flavor Text: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function.-The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function.),
(frameEffects:TEXT, frame Effects: The visual frame effects.-"colorshifted", "companion", "compasslanddfc", "devoid", "draft", "etched", "extendedart", "fullart", "inverted", "legendary", "lesson", "miracle", "mooneldrazidfc", "nyxtouched", "originpwdfc", "showcase", "snow", "sunmoondfc", "textless", "tombstone", "waxingandwaningmoondfc", Examples: [legendary, nyxtouched, miracle]),
(frameVersion:TEXT, frame Version: The version of the card frame style.-"1993", "1997", "2003", "2015", "future", Examples: [2003, 1993, 2015]),
(hand:TEXT, : The starting maximum hand size total modifier.-A + or - character precedes an integer.   positive maximum hand size: +1, +2, .... negative maximum hand size: -1, .... neural maximum hand size: 0...., Examples: [1, 0, -2]),
(hasAlternativeDeckLimit:INTEGER, has Alternative Deck Limit: If the card allows a value other than 4 copies in a deck.-0: disallow 1: allow, Examples: [0, 1]),
(hasContentWarning:INTEGER, has Content Warning: If the card marked by Wizards of the Coast (opens new window) for having sensitive content. See this official article (opens new window) for more information.-0: doesn't have 1: has sensitve content or Wizards of the Coast  Cards with this property may have missing or degraded properties and values., Examples: [0, 1]),
(hasFoil:INTEGER, has Foil: If the card can be found in foil-0: cannot be found 1: can be found, Examples: [0, 1]),
(hasNonFoil:INTEGER, has Non Foil: If the card can be found in non-foil-0: cannot be found 1: can be found, Examples: [1, 0]),
(isAlternative:INTEGER, is Alternative: If the card is an alternate variation to an original printing-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isFullArt:INTEGER, is Full Art: If the card has full artwork.-0: doesn't have, 1: has full artwork, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isOnlineOnly:INTEGER, is Online Only: If the card is only available in online game variations.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isOversized:INTEGER, is Oversized: If the card is oversized.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isPromo:INTEGER, is Promotion: If the card is a promotional printing.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isReprint:INTEGER, is Reprint: If the card has been reprinted.-0: has not 1: has not been, Examples: [1, 0]),
(isReserved:INTEGER, is Reserved: If the card is on the Magic: The Gathering Reserved List (opens new window)-If the card is on the Magic, it will appear in The Gathering Reserved List, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isStarter:INTEGER, is Starter: If the card is found in a starter deck such as Planeswalker/Brawl decks.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isStorySpotlight:INTEGER, is Story Spotlight: If the card is a Story Spotlight card.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isTextless:INTEGER, is Text less: If the card does not have a text box.-0: has a text box; 1: doesn't have a text box;, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isTimeshifted:INTEGER, is Time shifted: If the card is time shifted-If the card is "timeshifted", a feature of certain sets where a card will have a different frameVersion., Examples: [0, 1]),
(keywords:TEXT, : A list of keywords found on the card.-, Examples: [First strike, Flying, First strike,Flash]),
(layout:TEXT, : The type of card layout. For a token card, this will be "token"-, Examples: [normal, aftermath, split]),
(leadershipSkills:TEXT, leadership Skills: A list of formats the card is legal to be a commander in-),
(life:TEXT, : The starting life total modifier. A plus or minus character precedes an integer.-, Examples: [-5, -1, 2]),
(loyalty:TEXT, : The starting loyalty value of the card.-Used only on cards with "Planeswalker" in its types. empty means unkown, Examples: [6, 3, 4]),
(manaCost:TEXT, mana Cost: The mana cost of the card wrapped in brackets for each value.-manaCost is unconverted mana cost, Examples: [{5}{W}{W}, {4}{W}, {3}{W}]),
(mcmId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [16165, 16166, 16171]),
(mcmMetaId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [156, 176, 368]),
(mtgArenaId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [74983, 74986, 74987]),
(mtgjsonV4Id:TEXT, : -, Examples: [ad41be73-582f-58ed-abd4-a88c1f616ac3]),
(mtgoFoilId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [27501, 26993, 27473]),
(mtgoId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [27500, 26992, 27472]),
(multiverseId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [130550, 129465, 129470]),
(name:TEXT, : The name of the card.-Cards with multiple faces, like "Split" and "Meld" cards are given a delimiter., Examples: [Ancestor's Chosen, Angel of Mercy, Aven Cloudchaser]),
(number:TEXT, : The number of the card-, Examples: [1, 2, 7]),
(originalReleaseDate:TEXT, : original Release Date-The original release date in ISO 8601(opens new window) format for a promotional card printed outside of a cycle window, such as Secret Lair Drop promotions., Examples: [2012/12/1, 2006/12/1, 2007/12/1]),
(originalText:TEXT, : original Text-The text on the card as originally printed.),
(originalType:TEXT, : original Type-The type of the card as originally printed. Includes any supertypes and subtypes., Examples: [Creature - Human Cleric]),
(otherFaceIds:TEXT, : other Face Ids-A list of card UUID's to this card's counterparts, such as transformed or melded faces., Examples: [87f0062a-8321-5c16-960e-a12ce1df5839]),
(power:TEXT, : The power of the card.-∞ means infinite power null or * refers to unknown power, Examples: [4, 3, 2]),
(printings:TEXT, : A list of set printing codes the card was printed in, formatted in uppercase.-),
(promoTypes:TEXT, promo Types: A list of promotional types for a card.-"arenaleague", "boosterfun", "boxtopper", "brawldeck", "bundle", "buyabox", "convention", "datestamped", "draculaseries", "draftweekend", "duels", "event", "fnm", "gameday", "gateway", "giftbox", "gilded", "godzillaseries", "instore", "intropack", "jpwalker", "judgegift", "league", "mediainsert", "neonink", "openhouse", "planeswalkerstamped", "playerrewards", "playpromo", "premiereshop", "prerelease", "promopack", "release", "setpromo", "stamped", "textured", "themepack", "thick", "tourney", "wizardsplaynetwork", Examples: [boxtopper,boosterfun, boosterfun, release,buyabox]),
(purchaseUrls:TEXT, purchase Urls: Links that navigate to websites where the card can be purchased.-),
(rarity:TEXT, : The card printing rarity.-, Examples: [uncommon, common, rare]),
(scryfallId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [7a5cd03c-4227-4551-aa4b-7d119f0468b5]),
(scryfallIllustrationId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [be2f7173-c8b7-4172-a388-9b2c6b3c16e5]),
(scryfallOracleId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [fc2ccab7-cab1-4463-b73d-898070136d74]),
(setCode:TEXT, Set Code: The set printing code that the card is from.-, Examples: [10E, 2ED, 2XM]),
(side:TEXT, : The identifier of the card side.-Used on cards with multiple faces on the same card.  if this value is empty, then it means this card doesn't have multiple faces on the same card., Examples: [a, b, c]),
(subtypes:TEXT, : A list of card subtypes found after em-dash.-, Examples: [Human,Cleric, Angel, Bird,Soldier]),
(supertypes:TEXT, super types: A list of card supertypes found before em-dash.-list of all types should be the union of subtypes and supertypes, Examples: [Legendary, Basic, Legendary,Snow]),
(tcgplayerProductId:TEXT, tcg player ProductId: -, Examples: [15032, 15033, 15045]),
(text:TEXT, : The rules text of the card.-),
(toughness:TEXT, : The toughness of the card.-, Examples: [4, 3, 2]),
(type:TEXT, : The type of the card as visible, including any supertypes and subtypes.-"Artifact", "Card", "Conspiracy", "Creature", "Dragon", "Dungeon", "Eaturecray", "Elemental", "Elite", "Emblem", "Enchantment", "Ever", "Goblin", "Hero", "Instant", "Jaguar", "Knights", "Land", "Phenomenon", "Plane", "Planeswalker", "Scariest", "Scheme", "See", "Sorcery", "Sticker", "Summon", "Token", "Tribal", "Vanguard", "Wolf", "You’ll", "instant", Examples: [Creature — Human Cleric]),
(types:TEXT, : A list of all card types of the card, including Un‑sets and gameplay variants.-, Examples: [Creature, Instant, Enchantment]),
(uuid:TEXT, : The universal unique identifier (v5) generated by MTGJSON. Each entry is unique.-, Examples: [00010d56-fe38-5e35-8aed-518019aa36a5]),
(variations:TEXT, : -, Examples: [b7c19924-b4bf-56fc-aa73-f586e940bd42]),
(watermark:TEXT, : The name of the watermark on the card.-, Examples: [set (HOU), set (LGN), set (ONS)])
]
# Table: foreign_data
[
(id:INTEGER, : unique id number identifying this row of data-, Primary Key, Examples: [1, 2, 3]),
(flavorText:TEXT, flavor Text: The foreign flavor text of the card.-),
(language:TEXT, : The foreign language of card.-, Examples: [German, Spanish, French]),
(multiverseid:INTEGER, : The foreign multiverse identifier of the card.-, Examples: [148411, 150317, 149934]),
(name:TEXT, : The foreign name of the card.-, Examples: [Ausgewählter der Ahnfrau]),
(text:TEXT, : The foreign text ruling of the card.-),
(type:TEXT, : The foreign type of the card. Includes any supertypes and subtypes.-, Examples: [Kreatur — Mensch, Kleriker]),
(uuid:TEXT, : -, Examples: [5f8287b1-5bb6-5f4c-ad17-316a40d5bb0c])
]
# Table: legalities
[
(id:INTEGER, : unique id identifying this legality-, Primary Key, Examples: [1, 2, 3]),
(format:TEXT, : format of play-each value refers to different rules to play, Examples: [commander, duel, legacy]),
(status:TEXT, : -• legal • banned • restricted, Examples: [Legal, Banned, Restricted]),
(uuid:TEXT, : -, Examples: [5f8287b1-5bb6-5f4c-ad17-316a40d5bb0c])
]
# Table: rulings
[
(id:INTEGER, : unique id identifying this ruling-, Primary Key, Examples: [1, 2, 3]),
(date:DATE, : date-, Examples: [2007-07-15]),
(text:TEXT, : description about this ruling-),
(uuid:TEXT, : -, Examples: [6d268c95-c176-5766-9a46-c14f739aba1c])
]
# Table: set_translations
[
(id:INTEGER, : unique id identifying this set-, Primary Key, Examples: [1, 2, 3]),
(language:TEXT, : language of this card set-, Examples: [Chinese Simplified, Chinese Traditional, French]),
(setCode:TEXT, set code: the set code for this set-, Examples: [10E, 4ED, 5DN]),
(translation:TEXT, : translation of this card set-, Examples: [核心系列第十版])
]
# Table: sets
[
(id:INTEGER, : unique id identifying this set-, Primary Key, Examples: [1, 2, 3]),
(baseSetSize:INTEGER, base Set Size: The number of cards in the set.-, Examples: [383, 302, 332]),
(block:TEXT, : The block name the set was in.-, Examples: [Core Set, Mirrodin, Kaladesh]),

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T1.artist, T2.format
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN legalities AS T2
  ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid
WHERE
  T1.artist IN (
    SELECT
      artist
    FROM cards
    GROUP BY
      artist
    HAVING
      COUNT(id) = (
        SELECT
          MIN(card_count)
        FROM (
          SELECT
            COUNT(id) AS card_count
          FROM cards
          GROUP BY
            artist
        )
      )
  )
GROUP BY
  T1.artist,
  T2.format;

user_query: Find and list the names of sets which doesn't have Japanese translation but have Korean translation.

setCode.column_description: the set code for this set

format.value_description: each value refers to different rules to play

baseSetSize.column_description: The number of cards in the set.

block.column_description: The block name the set was in.

booster.column_description: A breakdown of possibilities and weights of cards in a booster pack.

code.column_description: The set code for the set.

isFoilOnly.column_description: If the set is only available in foil.

isForeignOnly.column_description: If the set is available only outside the United States of America.

isNonFoilOnly.column_description: If the set is only available in non-foil.

isOnlineOnly.column_description: If the set is only available in online game variations.

isPartialPreview.column_description: If the set is still in preview (spoiled). Preview sets do not have complete data.

keyruneCode.column_description: The matching Keyrune code for set image icons.

mcmIdExtras.column_description: The split Magic Card Market set identifier if a set is printed in two sets. This identifier represents the second set's identifier.

mtgoCode.column_description: The set code for the set as it appears on Magic: The Gathering Online
mtgoCode.value_description: if the value is null or empty, then it doesn't appear on Magic: The Gathering Online

parentCode.column_description: The parent set code for set variations like promotions, guild kits, etc.

releaseDate.column_description: The release date in ISO 8601 format for the set.

tcgplayerGroupId.column_description: The group identifier of the set on TCGplayer

totalSetSize.column_description: The total number of cards in the set, including promotional and related supplemental products but excluding Alchemy modifications - however those cards are included in the set itself.

type.column_description: The expansion type of the set.
type.value_description: "alchemy", "archenemy", "arsenal", "box", "commander", "core", "draft_innovation", "duel_deck", "expansion", "from_the_vault", "funny", "masterpiece", "masters", "memorabilia", "planechase", "premium_deck", "promo", "spellbook", "starter", "token", "treasure_chest", "vanguard"

text.column_description: description about this ruling

id.column_description: unique id number identifying this row of data

flavorText.column_description: The foreign flavor text of the card.

multiverseid.column_description: The foreign multiverse identifier of the card.

name.column_description: The foreign name of the card.

text.column_description: The foreign text ruling of the card.

type.column_description: The foreign type of the card. Includes any supertypes and subtypes.

id.column_name: unique id number identifying the cards

artist.column_description: The name of the artist that illustrated the card art.

asciiName.column_description: The ASCII(opens new window) (Basic/128) code formatted card name with no special unicode characters.

availability.column_description: A list of the card's available printing types.

borderColor.column_description: The color of the card border.

cardKingdomFoilId.value_description: cardKingdomFoilId, when paired with cardKingdomId that is not Null, is incredibly powerful.

cardKingdomId.value_description: A list of all the colors in the color indicator

colorIdentity.column_description: A list of all the colors found in manaCost, colorIndicator, and text

colorIndicator.column_description: A list of all the colors in the color indicator (The symbol prefixed to a card's types).

colors.column_description: A list of all the colors in manaCost and colorIndicator.
colors.value_description: Some cards may not have values, such as cards with "Devoid" in its text.

convertedManaCost.column_description: The converted mana cost of the card. Use the manaValue property.
convertedManaCost.value_description: if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana

duelDeck.column_description: The indicator for which duel deck the card is in.

faceConvertedManaCost.column_description: The converted mana cost or mana value for the face for either half or part of the card.

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to identify sets with Korean translations but without Japanese translations. This requires checking the 'language' column in the 'set_translations' table for both 'Korean' and the absence of 'Japanese'. The 'translation' column is also needed to retrieve the name of the set.

The question asks to find sets that have Korean translation but do not have Japanese translation. The `set_translations` table contains information about translations for sets, including the language and the translation itself. The `sets` table contains the set `name` and `code`. To answer the question, I need to: 1. Identify sets that have a Korean translation. This requires checking the `language` column in `set_translations`. 2. Identify sets that do not have a Japanese translation. This also requires checking the `language` column in `set_translations`. 3. Join `set_translations` with `sets` to get the set names. The `setCode` in `set_translations` links to the `code` in `sets`. Therefore, I need `set_translations.language`, `set_translations.setCode`, `sets.code`, and `sets.name`.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.name FROM sets AS T1 WHERE T1.code IN (SELECT setCode FROM set_translations WHERE language = 'Korean') AND T1.code NOT IN (SELECT setCode FROM set_translations WHERE language = 'Japanese')

This requires joining the `superhero` table with the `hero_power` table to link superheroes to their powers. 2. Filter these counts to include only those superheroes with more than 15 powers. 3. To find the tallest hero, I need to access the `height_cm` column in the `superhero` table and find the maximum value. To filter for heroes published by 'Marvel Comics', I need to join the `superhero` table with the `publisher` table using `publisher_id` and filter by `publisher_name` being 'Marvel Comics'. sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T1.full_name
FROM superhero AS T1
INNER JOIN publisher AS T2
  ON T1.publisher_id = T2.id
WHERE
  T2.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics'
ORDER BY
  T1.height_cm DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 1;

The question asks to identify the publisher of the slowest superhero. The hint specifies that 'slowest superhero' refers to the minimum 'Speed' attribute value and 'publisher' refers to 'publisher_name'. Therefore, I need to find the superhero with the minimum speed, which requires joining the `superhero` table with the `hero_attribute` table to get the speed attribute. Then, I need to join with the `publisher` table to get the publisher's name. The `hero_attribute` table contains `attribute_name` and `attribute_value` to identify the speed and its value. The `superhero` table links heroes to publishers via `publisher_id`. The `publisher` table contains the `publisher_name`.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT
  T3.publisher_name
FROM hero_attribute AS T1
INNER JOIN superhero AS T2
  ON T1.hero_id = T2.id
INNER JOIN publisher AS T3
  ON T2.publisher_id = T3.id
WHERE
  T1.attribute_id = 1 -- Assumed attribute_id for 'Speed' based on the hint and missing 'attribute' table.
ORDER BY
  T1.attribute_value ASC
LIMIT 1;

Identify the 'strength' attribute. 2. Find the hero associated with this attribute. 3. Retrieve the hero's name. The `attribute` table is needed to find the ID for 'strength'. The `hero_attribute` table is needed to link heroes to attributes and find the maximum attribute value. The `superhero` table is needed to get the superhero's name. Since there's no direct 'attribute_value' in `hero_attribute`, it's likely that the presence of a hero in `hero_attribute` with the 'strength' attribute signifies having that attribute. Therefore, we need to find heroes who have the 'strength' attribute and then select their names. The `attribute_name` column in the `attribute` table is essential to filter for 'strength'. The `hero_id` column in `hero_attribute` is needed to link to the `superhero` table. The `attribute_id` in `hero_attribute` is needed to join with the `attribute` table. The `id` column in `superhero` is needed to join with `hero_attribute`. The `superhero_name` column in `superhero` is needed to display the hero's name. Given the hint and schema, it's most probable that 'highest attribute in strength' means finding heroes who possess the 'strength' attribute, and among those, selecting one. The question asks to calculate the percentage of times Hamilton was not in the 1st position at the first track of the F1 circuit since 2010. This requires identifying Hamilton's driver information, filtering races by year (>= 2010), identifying the first track, and then checking Hamilton's finishing position in those races. The hint also guides us to count races where Hamilton's surname is 'Hamilton', the year is >= 2010, and his position is greater than 1 (not first). sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.position > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T2.raceId)
FROM drivers AS T1
INNER JOIN results AS T2
  ON T1.driverId = T2.driverId
INNER JOIN races AS T3
  ON T2.raceId = T3.raceId
WHERE
  T1.surname = 'Hamilton' AND T3.year >= 2010;

sql_exec_info.sql:
WITH RaceInfo AS (
    SELECT raceId
    FROM races
    WHERE name = '2008 Australian Grand Prix'
),
-- CTE to parse absolute times (HH:MM:SS.ms) into milliseconds
-- This is used to find the true champion's time
AbsoluteTimeParser AS (
    SELECT
        T1.raceId,
        T1.driverId, -- Include driverId for joining later
        T1.time AS time_str,
        INSTR(T1.time, ':') AS first_colon_pos,
        -- Calculate relative position of second colon in the substring after the first colon
        INSTR(SUBSTR(T1.time, INSTR(T1.time, ':') + 1), ':') AS second_colon_rel_pos,
        INSTR(T1.time, '.') AS dot_pos
    FROM results AS T1
    INNER JOIN RaceInfo ON T1.raceId = RaceInfo.raceId
    WHERE T1.time NOT LIKE '+%' AND T1.time IS NOT NULL
),
AbsoluteTimesInMs AS (
    SELECT
        raceId,
        driverId,
        time_str,
        (
            CAST(SUBSTR(time_str, 1, first_colon_pos - 1) AS INTEGER) * 3600000 + -- Hours
            CAST(SUBSTR(time_str, first_colon_pos + 1, second_colon_rel_pos - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60000 + -- Minutes
            -- Corrected INSTR usage for seconds part:
            -- Calculate absolute position of the second colon, then extract seconds
            CAST(SUBSTR(time_str,
                        (first_colon_pos + second_colon_rel_pos) + 1,
                        dot_pos - ((first_colon_pos + second_colon_rel_pos) + 1)
                   ) AS INTEGER) * 1000 + -- Seconds
            CAST(SUBSTR(time_str, dot_pos + 1) AS INTEGER) -- Milliseconds
        ) AS parsed_absolute_ms
    FROM AbsoluteTimeParser
),
-- Champion's time is the minimum of all absolute times for the race
ChampionTimeMs AS (
    SELECT MIN(parsed_absolute_ms) AS champion_ms
    FROM AbsoluteTimesInMs
),
-- Convert all driver times (absolute and relative) to absolute milliseconds
AllDriverAbsoluteTimes AS (
    SELECT
        T1.driverId,
        T1.time AS time_str,
        (SELECT champion_ms FROM ChampionTimeMs) AS champion_base_ms,
        CASE
            -- If it's an absolute time (not prefixed with '+'), use the pre-parsed value
            WHEN T1.time NOT LIKE '+%' THEN ATIM.parsed_absolute_ms
            -- If it's a relative time in +M:SS.ms format
            WHEN T1.time LIKE '+%:%' THEN
                (SELECT champion_ms FROM ChampionTimeMs) +
                (
                    CAST(SUBSTR(T1.time, 2, INSTR(SUBSTR(T1.time, 2), ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60000 + -- Minutes
                    CAST(SUBSTR(T1.time, INSTR(T1.time, ':') + 1, INSTR(SUBSTR(T1.time, INSTR(T1.time, ':') + 1), '.') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 1000 + -- Seconds
                    CAST(SUBSTR(T1.time, INSTR(T1.time, '.') + 1) AS INTEGER) -- Milliseconds
                )
            -- If it's a relative time in +S.ms format
            WHEN T1.time LIKE '+%' THEN
                (SELECT champion_ms FROM ChampionTimeMs) +
                (
                    CAST(SUBSTR(T1.time, 2, INSTR(T1.time, '.') - 2) AS INTEGER) * 1000 + -- Seconds
                    CAST(SUBSTR(T1.time, INSTR(T1.time, '.') + 1) AS INTEGER) -- Milliseconds
                )
            ELSE NULL
        END AS absolute_time_ms
    FROM results AS T1
    INNER JOIN RaceInfo ON T1.raceId = RaceInfo.raceId
    -- Left join to get pre-parsed absolute times for drivers who have them
    LEFT JOIN AbsoluteTimesInMs AS ATIM ON T1.raceId = ATIM.raceId AND T1.driverId = ATIM.driverId AND T1.time = ATIM.time_str
    WHERE T1.time IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    (MAX(absolute_time_ms) - (SELECT champion_ms FROM ChampionTimeMs)) * 100.0 / MAX(absolute_time_ms)
FROM AllDriverAbsoluteTimes;

FROM lapTimes AS T1

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: The question asks for the name of the league with the highest number of matches and the count of those matches. To achieve this, I need to: 1. Count the number of matches for each league. The `Match` table contains `league_id` which can be used to group matches by league. 2. Join the `Match` table with the `League` table using `league_id` to get the `name` of the league. 3. Order the results by the match count in descending order and select the top one to find the league with the highest number of matches. Therefore, `Match.league_id` is needed to count matches per league, and `League.name` is needed to display the league's name. `Match.league_id` also serves as the join key to `League.id` (assuming `League.id` is the primary key for `League` and `Match.league_id` is the foreign key, though `League.id` is not explicitly defined in the schema, it's implied by the foreign key constraint).

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.name, COUNT(T2.league_id) FROM League AS T1 INNER JOIN Match AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.league_id GROUP BY T1.name ORDER BY COUNT(T2.league_id) DESC LIMIT 1

The team_long_name column is needed for the final output. The buildUpPlayPassing column is needed to filter based on the average. The team_api_id is needed to join the tables. The team_fifa_api_id is needed to join the tables. The buildUpPlayPassingClass column is needed to filter based on the passing class. The buildUpPlayPassing column is needed to calculate the average.

The question asks for the long name of teams with above-average build-up play passing in 2012. This requires joining the 'Team' table (for team long name) with the 'Team_Attributes' table (for build-up play passing). The hint specifies filtering for the year 2012, which implies a date column is needed, but the provided schema for 'Match' does not have a date column. However, the hint mentions 'in 2012 refers to strftime('%Y', date) = '2012'', suggesting that a date column is implicitly assumed to be available or derivable. Since no date column is present in the schema, I will proceed assuming the 'Match' table has a date column, and it's the only place it could logically reside. The 'buildUpPlayPassing' column is needed to calculate the average and filter for above-average values. The 'team_long_name' is the output requested. The 'team_api_id' is needed to join 'Team' and 'Team_Attributes'. The 'team_fifa_api_id' is also present in both tables and could be used for joining, but 'team_api_id' is a more direct link if available in both. The hint also mentions 'WHERE buildUpPlayPassing IS NOT NULL', so this column is crucial for filtering. sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT T1.team_long_name
FROM Team AS T1
INNER JOIN Team_Attributes AS T2
  ON T1.team_api_id = T2.team_api_id
WHERE
  STRFTIME('%Y', T2.date) = '2012' AND T2.buildUpPlayPassing IS NOT NULL
  AND T2.buildUpPlayPassing > (
    SELECT AVG(T3.buildUpPlayPassing)
    FROM Team_Attributes AS T3
    WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T3.date) = '2012' AND T3.buildUpPlayPassing IS NOT NULL
  );

The team_long_name column is needed for the final output. The buildUpPlayPassing column is needed to filter based on the average. The team_api_id is needed to join the tables. The team_fifa_api_id is needed to join the tables. The buildUpPlayPassingClass column is needed to filter based on the passing class. sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT T1.team_long_name
FROM Team AS T1
INNER JOIN Team_Attributes AS T2
  ON T1.team_api_id = T2.team_api_id
WHERE
  STRFTIME('%Y', T2.date) = '2012' AND T2.buildUpPlayPassing > (
    SELECT
      AVG(buildUpPlayPassing)
    FROM Team_Attributes
    WHERE
      STRFTIME('%Y', date) = '2012'
  );

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Filter players by height > 180, 2) Calculate the average heading accuracy for each player, 3) Order the players by average heading accuracy in descending order, and 4) Limit the results to the top 10. The player_name column is needed to display the player's name. The height column is needed to filter players with height above 180. The heading_accuracy column is needed to calculate the average heading accuracy. The player_fifa_api_id is needed to calculate the average heading accuracy.

The question asks for the top 10 players' names whose heights are above 180, ordered by their average heading accuracy. To achieve this, I need to: 1. Filter players by height greater than 180. The `Player` table contains the `height` column. 2. Calculate the average heading accuracy for these players. The `Player_Attributes` table contains the `heading_accuracy` column and `player_fifa_api_id` which can be used to group and average. 3. Select the player names from the `Player` table. 4. Join `Player` and `Player_Attributes` tables using a common identifier (likely `player_fifa_api_id` or `player_api_id` if it existed in `Player`). Based on the schema, it seems `player_fifa_api_id` is the link. 5. Order the results by the calculated average heading accuracy in descending order and limit to 10.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.player_name FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T1.height > 180 GROUP BY T1.player_name ORDER BY AVG(T2.heading_accuracy) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Filter players by height > 180, 2) Calculate the average heading accuracy for each player, 3) Order the players by average heading accuracy in descending order, and 4) Limit the results to the top 10. The player_name column is needed to display the player's name. The height column is needed to filter players with height above 180. The heading_accuracy column is needed to calculate the average heading accuracy. The player_fifa_api_id is needed to calculate the average heading accuracy.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT
          T1.player_name
        FROM Player AS T1
        INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2
          ON T1.player_fifa_api_id = T2.player_fifa_api_id
        WHERE
          T1.height > 180
        GROUP BY
          T1.player_name
        ORDER BY
          AVG(T2.heading_accuracy) DESC
        LIMIT 10;

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to find Aaron Doran's potential score. I need to access the Player table to filter by player name and the Player_Attributes table to retrieve the potential score. The foreign keys will be used to join these two tables.

The question asks for the 'potential' score of a player named 'Aaron Doran'. I need to find the 'potential' column in the 'Player_Attributes' table and the 'player_name' column in the 'Player' table to filter for the specific player. The 'player_name' column in the 'Player' table is used to identify the player, and the 'potential' column in the 'Player_Attributes' table contains the score we are looking for. I will need to join these two tables on player_api_id or player_fifa_api_id to link the player's name to their attributes.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T2.potential FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T1.player_name = 'Aaron Doran' ORDER BY T2.date DESC LIMIT 1

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: The question asks to identify the players who perform the best in crossing actions among Alexis, Ariel Borysiuk and Arouna Kone. This requires finding the maximum crossing score for these players. The player_name column is needed to identify the specific players. The crossing column is needed to determine the crossing ability. The player_fifa_api_id or player_api_id is needed to link the player name to the player attributes.

The question asks to identify which of three specific players (Alexis, Ariel Borysiuk, or Arouna Kone) performs best in crossing actions. The hint indicates that 'best in crossing actions' refers to the maximum value in the 'crossing' column. Therefore, I need to: 1) Access player names to filter for the specified players. 2) Access the 'crossing' attribute for these players to determine who has the highest value. The 'Player' table contains player names, and the 'Player_Attributes' table contains player crossing abilities. I will need to join these tables on player ID to link names to attributes.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.player_name FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE (T1.player_name LIKE '%Alexis%' OR T1.player_name = 'Ariel Borysiuk' OR T1.player_name = 'Arouna Kone') ORDER BY T2.crossing DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to filter players by height and volley score. The Player table contains the height information, and the Player_Attributes table contains the volley score. The question requires joining these tables using player_api_id.

The question asks to count players based on two criteria: height and volley score. The `Player` table contains the `height` column, and the `Player_Attributes` table contains the `volleys` column. Both tables are linked by `player_api_id` or `player_fifa_api_id`, which are foreign keys to the `Player` table. Therefore, I need to join these two tables and filter based on the conditions provided in the hint.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.player_api_id) FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T1.height > 180 AND T2.volleys > 70

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: The question asks for players with a 'high' attacking work rate. Therefore, we need to access the Player table to retrieve the player's name and the Player_Attributes table to filter by attacking_work_rate.

The question asks for players who tend to be attacking when their teammates are also attacking. The hint specifies that 'tend to be attacking' corresponds to the `attacking_work_rate` being 'high'. To identify these players, I need to access the `Player_Attributes` table to filter by `attacking_work_rate`. Since the question asks for the players' names, I will also need to join with the `Player` table using `player_api_id` to retrieve the `player_name`. The `player_fifa_api_id` in `Player_Attributes` is the foreign key to `Player`'s `player_api_id`.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T1.player_name FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T2.attacking_work_rate = 'high'

# Table: Player
[
(player_name:TEXT, player name: player name-, Examples: [Aaron Appindangoye, Aaron Cresswell, Aaron Doran])
]
# Table: Player_Attributes
[
(attacking_work_rate:TEXT, attacking work rate: the player's attacking work rate-commonsense reasoning:  • high: implies that the player is going to be in all of your attack moves • medium: implies that the player will select the attack actions he will join in • low: remain in his position while the team attacks, Examples: [medium, high, low])
]
【Foreign keys】
Player_Attributes.player_api_id=Player.player_api_id
Player_Attributes.player_fifa_api_id=Player.player_fifa_api_id

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: The question asks for players who tend to be attacking when their teammates are also attacking. The hint specifies that 'tend to be attacking' corresponds to the `attacking_work_rate` being 'high'. To identify these players, I need to access the `Player_Attributes` table to filter by `attacking_work_rate`. Since the question asks for the players' names, I will also need to join with the `Player` table using `player_api_id` to retrieve the `player_name`. The `player_fifa_api_id` in `Player_Attributes` is the foreign key to `Player`'s `player_api_id`.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.player_name FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T2.attacking_work_rate = 'high'

【DB_ID】 european_football_2
【Schema】
# Table: Player
[
(player_api_id:INTEGER, player api id: the id of the player api-, Examples: [2625, 2752, 2768]),
(player_name:TEXT, player name: player name-, Examples: [Aaron Appindangoye, Aaron Cresswell, Aaron Doran])
]
# Table: Player_Attributes
[
(player_fifa_api_id:INTEGER, player federation international football association api id: the id of the player fifa api-, Examples: [218353, 189615, 186170]),
(attacking_work_rate:TEXT, attacking work rate: the player's attacking work rate-commonsense reasoning:  • high: implies that the player is going to be in all of your attack moves • medium: implies that the player will select the attack actions he will join in • low: remain in his position while the team attacks, Examples: [medium, high, low])
]
【Foreign keys】
Player_Attributes.player_api_id=Player.player_api_id
Player_Attributes.player_fifa_api_id=Player.player_fifa_api_id
schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: The question asks for players who tend to be attacking when their teammates are also attacking. The hint specifies that 'tend to be attacking' corresponds to the `attacking_work_rate` being 'high'. To identify these players, I need to access the `Player_Attributes` table to filter by `attacking_work_rate`. Since the question asks for the players' names, I will also need to join with the `Player` table using `player_api_id` to retrieve the `player_name`. The `player_fifa_api_id` in `Player_Attributes` is the foreign key to `Player`'s `player_api_id`.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T1.player_name FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T2.attacking_work_rate = 'high'

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer the question, I need to identify patients born in 1937 and check their total cholesterol. Therefore, I need the birthday from the Patient table and the total cholesterol from the Laboratory table. The ID column is needed to join the two tables.

The question asks to list patients born in 1937 with total cholesterol beyond the normal range. To achieve this, I need to: 1) Filter patients by their birth year (1937) using the 'Birthday' column in the 'Patient' table. 2) Filter laboratory results for 'T-CHO' greater than or equal to 250, which is in the 'Laboratory' table. 3) Join the 'Patient' and 'Laboratory' tables on the 'ID' column to link patient birth dates with their cholesterol levels. 4) Select the patient IDs to list the patients.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T1.ID FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T1.Birthday) = '1937' AND T2."T-CHO" >= 250

Identify patients who are 'in-patients' using the 'Admission' column in the 'Patient' table. 2. Calculate the age of these patients using their 'Birthday' from the 'Patient' table and the current timestamp. 3. Filter patients who are 50 years or older. 4. schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: The question asks for the average 'aCL IgG' concentration for in-patients aged 50 and above. To achieve this, I need to: 1. Identify patients who are 'in-patients' using the 'Admission' column in the 'Patient' table. 2. Calculate the age of these patients using their 'Birthday' from the 'Patient' table and the current timestamp. 3. Filter patients who are 50 years or older. 4. Join the 'Patient' table with the 'Examination' table using the 'ID' column to access the 'aCL IgG' values. 5. Calculate the average of the 'aCL IgG' for the filtered patients. Therefore, the relevant columns are 'Admission' and 'Birthday' from the 'Patient' table, and 'ID' and 'aCL IgG' from the 'Examination' table.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT AVG(T1."aCL IgG") FROM Examination AS T1 INNER JOIN Patient AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.Admission = '+' AND (STRFTIME('%Y', 'now') - STRFTIME('%Y', T2.Birthday)) >= 50

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer the question, I need to find the patient with the specified 'First Date' and 'Diagnosis'. Then, I need to count the number of laboratory tests for that patient in 1995. Therefore, I need columns from 'Patient' and 'Laboratory' tables, and the 'Examination' table is not needed because the question doesn't mention it. The 'ID' column is needed to link the tables, 'First Date' and 'Diagnosis' are needed to identify the patient, and 'Date' is needed to filter the lab tests.

The question asks for the total number of laboratory tests for a specific patient in a specific year. First, I need to identify the patient based on their first visit date and diagnosis. The `Patient` table contains `First Date` and `Diagnosis` to identify the patient, and also the `ID` to link to their laboratory tests. Then, I need to count the laboratory tests for that patient in the year 1995. The `Laboratory` table contains the `ID` to link to the patient and the `Date` to filter by year. The `ID` column in `Laboratory` is also what needs to be counted.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Laboratory AS T1 WHERE T1.ID = (SELECT ID FROM Patient WHERE "First Date" = '1991-06-13' AND Diagnosis = 'SJS') AND STRFTIME('%Y', T1.Date) = '1995'

First, I need to identify the patient based on their first visit date and diagnosis. The `Patient` table contains `First Date` and `Diagnosis` to identify the patient, and also the `ID` to link to their laboratory tests. Then, I need to count the laboratory tests for that patient in the year 1995. The `Laboratory` table contains the `ID` to link to the patient and the `Date` to filter by year. The `ID` column in `Laboratory` is also what needs to be counted.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Laboratory AS T1 WHERE T1.ID = (SELECT T2.ID FROM Patient AS T2 WHERE T2.`First Date` = '1991-06-13' AND T2.Diagnosis = 'SJS') AND STRFTIME('%Y', T1.Date) = '1995'

The SEX column is needed to filter for female patients. The Diagnosis column is needed to filter for patients diagnosed with SLE. The ID column is needed to join the tables. The ALB column is needed for the average calculation.

The question asks for the average blood albumin level (ALB) for female patients (SEX = 'F') diagnosed with SLE (Diagnosis = 'SLE') and who have a PLT greater than 400. This requires joining the Patient table (for SEX and Diagnosis) with the Laboratory table (for ALB and PLT). The 'Patient' table is needed to filter by 'SEX' and 'Diagnosis'. The 'Laboratory' table is needed to filter by 'PLT' and to calculate the average of 'ALB'. The ID column is needed to join the two tables.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT AVG(T1.ALB) FROM Laboratory AS T1 INNER JOIN Patient AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.SEX = 'F' AND T1.PLT > 400 AND T2.Diagnosis = 'SLE'

The question asks for the highest anti-nucleus antibody concentration level (ANA) of a patient with a normal creatinine level (CRE < 1.5). To answer this, I need to: 1. Select the maximum value from the 'ANA' column in the 'Examination' table. 2. Filter the results based on the 'CRE' column in the 'Laboratory' table, specifically where 'CRE' is less than 1.5. 3. Join the 'Examination' and 'Laboratory' tables on the 'ID' column to link patient examinations with their laboratory results.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT MAX(T1.ANA) FROM Examination AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.CRE < 1.5

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Calculate the average parking cost. This requires identifying parking expenses and summing their costs and dividing by the number of events. 2) Identify the events with parking costs less than the calculated average. The event_name is needed for the final output. The budget table contains the category and the spent amount, which is used to calculate the average parking cost. The event table is needed to get the event name and link to budget table.

The question asks for event names with less than the average parking cost. To achieve this, I need to: 1. Identify expenses related to 'Parking' from the 'budget' table. 2. Calculate the total cost of 'Parking' expenses and the total number of 'Parking' expenses to determine the average parking cost. 3. Join the 'expense' table with the 'budget' table on 'link_to_budget' to link expenses to their budget categories. 4. Join the 'expense' table with the 'event' table using the 'link_to_event' column in the 'expense' table and 'event_id' (implicitly from the foreign key constraint) in the 'event' table to get the event names. 5. Filter for events where the parking cost is less than the calculated average parking cost. The 'event_name' is needed for the final output. The 'cost' column is needed to calculate the average parking cost and to filter events. The 'category' column in the 'budget' table is needed to filter for 'Parking' expenses. The 'link_to_budget' in the 'expense' table and 'budget_id' in the 'budget' table are needed for joining. The 'link_to_event' in the 'expense' table and 'event_id' (implicitly) in the 'event' table are needed for joining.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.event_name FROM event AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event WHERE T2.category = 'Parking' AND T2.spent < (SELECT AVG(spent) FROM budget WHERE category = 'Parking')

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To calculate the percentage of cost for game events, I need to identify game events, sum their costs, and then calculate the percentage. The event table provides the event type, and the expense table provides the cost. The link between them is the event_id, which is found in the budget table.

The question asks for the percentage of the cost for 'game' events. This requires joining the 'event' table to filter for 'Game' types and the 'budget' table to get the cost associated with these events. The 'type' column in the 'event' table is needed to filter for 'Game' events. The 'link_to_event' column in the 'budget' table is needed to join with the 'event' table. The 'spent' column in the 'budget' table contains the cost information. The hint also mentions 'percentage = DIVIDE( SUM(cost), COUNT(event_id)) * 100', which implies we need to sum the costs and count the events. The 'event_id' is implicitly available through the foreign key relationship from 'budget.link_to_event' to 'event.event_id'. Therefore, we need 'event.type', 'budget.spent', and 'budget.link_to_event' to link the tables and calculate the percentage.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT (SUM(T3.cost) * 100.0) / COUNT(DISTINCT T1.event_id)
FROM event AS T1
INNER JOIN budget AS T2
  ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event
INNER JOIN expense AS T3
  ON T2.budget_id = T3.link_to_budget
WHERE T1.type = 'Game'

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Filter the 'yearmonth' table for the year 2012. 2) Filter the 'customers' table for the segment 'LAM'. 3) Join these tables to link consumption with customer segment. 4) Find the customer with the least consumption. The 'Date' column in 'yearmonth' is needed to filter for the year 2012. The 'Consumption' column in 'yearmonth' is needed to identify the least consumption. The 'Segment' column in 'customers' is needed to filter for the segment 'LAM'.

The question asks for the customer with the least consumption in 'LAM' during the year 2012. To answer this, I need to: 1) Filter for the year 2012. The `yearmonth` table has a `Date` column that can be used for this, and the hint suggests a range. 2) Filter for the segment 'LAM'. The `customers` table has a `Segment` column. 3) Join `yearmonth` and `customers` tables to link consumption data with customer segments. 4) Find the minimum `Consumption` within the filtered data. The `CustomerID` is the linking column between `yearmonth` and `customers`. The `yearmonth.Date` is needed to filter by year. The `customers.Segment` is needed to filter by 'LAM'. The `yearmonth.Consumption` is needed to find the least consumption. The `yearmonth.CustomerID` and `customers.CustomerID` are needed for the join. The `customers.Segment` column has 'LAM' as an example, and `yearmonth.Date` can be filtered for the year 2012. The `yearmonth.Consumption` column has examples of consumption values.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.CustomerID FROM customers AS T1 INNER JOIN yearmonth AS T2 ON T1.CustomerID = T2.CustomerID WHERE T1.Segment = 'LAM' AND T2.Date BETWEEN '201201' AND '201212' GROUP BY T1.CustomerID ORDER BY SUM(T2.Consumption) ASC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1
